summary.en-US: Unofficial: answer WaniKani reviews and lesson quizzes by voice, on desktop or Android. Speech recognition runs entirely on your device; nothing is sent anywhere. Hiragana readings and English meanings. Created with AI: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5.

description.en-US: Say your WaniKani answers instead of typing them. Hold Shift (or, on a phone, the mic button), say the meaning or the reading, and release: the answer is filled into WaniKani's answer box, ready for you to submit. Private by design • Speech recognition runs inside Firefox on your own computer or phone. Your voice is never sent anywhere: the extension makes no network requests at all, and its speech models ship inside the add-on. • It never reads the question. It only checks whether WaniKani is asking for a meaning or a reading, so a wrong answer goes in exactly as you said it. • No account, no tracking, no data collection. Permissions: WaniKani pages and local storage only. Features • English meanings and radical names (Moonshine, fast, by default; or OpenAI Whisper, accurate). • Readings in hiragana, from a speech model that writes kana directly, so it never has to guess a reading from kanji. • Alternatives: if it also heard something else (hand / and, じん / にん), press its number (or tap it) to switch before submitting. Choose 1 to 5 choices, separately for English and readings. Impossible kana spellings are never offered. • Push-to-talk (Shift, configurable) or hands-free. • Fill only, or fill and submit; optional auto-advance (or only after a correct answer). • Works in reviews and lesson quizzes. • Firefox for Android: everything works by touch (hold the mic button to talk, at the left end of the panel or, if you prefer, the right; Submit, Clear and Next buttons), and the panel stays above the on-screen keyboard. • Optional WaniKani dictionary: answers that are the meaning or reading of any WaniKani item are offered first. You make the dictionary file with a script from the source repository and your own WaniKani API token; the add-on itself never goes online. • Optional: ignore a wrong answer you submitted by accident (Escape or Backspace, or tap Ignore). The question comes back unanswered and WaniKani doesn't count the mistake, like the Double-Check script's re-type. • Optional activity log, for training your own models: what was heard, which choice you picked, whether WaniKani marked it correct and how long each question took, kept as text on your device (no audio, never the question; at most 10,000 entries) until you clear or export it. • Advanced: load your own fine-tuned model per language. Tools to fine-tune on your own voice are in the source repository. Requirements No GPU needed: everything runs on the CPU. On a fast desktop answers take about 0.1 s (English, fast), 1.5 s (English, accurate) and 0.4 s (readings); on a Pixel 9 Pro XL about 0.3 s, 4 s and 0.5 s. The models use about 430 MB of memory while a review is open (720 MB with accurate English). Firefox 140+ on desktop, 142+ on Android; the download is about 165 MB. Avoid system noise gates or suppressors on the microphone (e.g. EasyEffects): they cut off the start of words. Notes An unofficial tool: not affiliated with or endorsed by WaniKani or Tofugu. Open source (MIT). This extension was created with AI: all of its code was written by Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 (in Claude Code), directed and tested by a human.

release_notes.en-US:
On phones and tablets the mic button is now at the left end of the panel, within reach of your thumb, with the choices and Submit / Next on that side too. Settings → Panel → Mic button on touch screens puts it back on the right. Nothing changes with a mouse or keyboard.

Activity log (optional, off by default): each answer also notes how long the question took, and tools/analyze-log.mjs in the source repository reports the time per question, leaving out the times you'd stepped away. The log now keeps at most 10,000 entries (about 3,000 questions); past that, the oldest are dropped.

As always, nothing leaves your device, the question is never read, and a wrong answer goes in exactly as you said it.
